name: Jean Baptiste Andre Dumas
summary: Outstanding experimental chemist who directed the study of organic chemistry in the second quarter of the 19th century.

name: Alais
summary: Industrial city in France's Departement du Gard where Dumas was born.

name: Geneva
summary: Swiss city where Dumas studied pharmacy and began his scientific career.

name: Paris
summary: French capital where Dumas established his career in chemistry and academia.

name: Le Royer and Tingry
summary: Pharmacy in Geneva where Dumas was apprenticed and conducted early research.

name: Société de Physique et d'Histoire Naturelle de Genève
aliases: Society of Physics and Natural History of Geneva
summary: Scientific society in Geneva where Dumas became a member and presented memoirs.

name: Ecole Polytechnique
summary: Engineering school in Paris where Dumas served as Répétiteur.

name: Athénée Royale de Paris
summary: Educational institution in Paris where Dumas worked as Préparateur and Professor.

name: College de France
summary: Higher education institution in Paris where Dumas gave influential courses on chemical philosophy.

name: Academy of Sciences
summary: Prestigious French scientific academy to which Dumas was elected in 1832.

name: Faculty of Sciences
summary: Paris faculty where Dumas was appointed professor of chemistry.

name: Faculty of Medicine
summary: Paris faculty where Dumas was appointed professor of organic chemistry and pharmacy.

name: Ecole Centrale des Arts et Manufactures
summary: Industrial school founded with Dumas's predominant role.

name: Jean Louis Prévost
summary: Genevan physician and physiologist who collaborated with Dumas on blood and generation research.

name: Augustin Pyramus De Candolle
summary: Botanist and teacher in Geneva who influenced Dumas's approach to classification.

name: Gaspard De la Rive
summary: Chemist and teacher in Geneva who popularized atomic theory to Dumas.

name: Nicolas Théodore de Saussure
summary: Plant physiologist and mentor who guided Dumas's interest in organic chemistry.

name: Montyon Prize
summary: Annual prize in experimental physiology awarded by the Royal Academy of Sciences.

name: Traité de Chimie appliquée aux Arts
summary: Dumas's textbook in applied chemistry published in eight volumes.

name: Law of Substitution
summary: Chemical theory developed by Dumas regarding the chlorination of organic compounds.

name: Type Theory
summary: Chemical classification theory developed by Dumas replacing the Ether Theory.
